work.title: ROUNDTABLE BRIEF
work.subtitle: 融资圆桌问答稿
work.scope: Fictional fundraising speech template. Spoken drafts, ventures, people and illustrative models are invented; no real traction, validated impact, technical performance, securities offer, investment terms or committed funding is supplied.

pages.title: What are you building?
pages.lead: We are exploring Common Page, a fictional concept for keeping a discussion question beside the material it refers to. The aim is a more inspectable conversation. This is a concept explanation, not a claim that a deployed product or a real company has been established.
pages.body: Follow-up: what would a first useful artifact demonstrate? Keep a short answer available before adding detail. The module index is a navigation aid, not a timed agenda or a record of an actual investor meeting.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: What is the smallest claim that accurately describes the current concept?

records.label: Short answer
records.prompt: Common Page is a fictional shared-context document concept.

records.label: Evidence boundary
records.prompt: No operating product or customer activity established.

records.label: Follow-up question
records.prompt: Which task needs its context kept visible?

pages.title: Why does this problem matter?
pages.lead: A reference can be hard to interpret when its intended use is missing. That is our working premise. We would need appropriate evidence about a defined context before calling it a recurring need, a market opportunity or a reason that a real customer should pay.
pages.body: Follow-up: whose task are we discussing? Do not replace evidence with a founder’s confidence or a fictional anecdote presented as a testimonial.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: Which source would make the problem statement more than a plausible story?

records.label: Problem premise
records.prompt: Shared material can become difficult to interpret later.

records.label: Relevant context
records.prompt: Understand the original task and the later reader's need.

records.label: Source to seek
records.prompt: Seek appropriate observations, not an invented testimonial.

pages.title: What would the product actually do?
pages.lead: The proposed experience connects a passage, a question and a source note. That is an intended workflow. We have not supplied a working implementation, a validated user journey or a capability benchmark, so we should not imply that the illustration demonstrates those things.
pages.body: Follow-up: which interaction is most uncertain? Use a clearly labelled concept artifact when available; do not describe an editorial image as a product screenshot.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: Which capability could you responsibly demonstrate today?

records.label: Proposed workflow
records.prompt: Keep material beside its purpose and review questions.

records.label: Unverified capability
records.prompt: Implementation and reliability have not been demonstrated.

records.label: Demonstration needed
records.prompt: An inspectable interaction with explicit limitations.

pages.title: What do you know about the market?
pages.lead: We have not supplied a market study or a verified market-size estimate. The useful starting question is which organisation has this task, what alternatives it already uses and under what conditions a different approach would matter. We should earn a market claim through relevant sources.
pages.body: Follow-up: what is the credible manual alternative? No competitor performance, customer segment size or growth rate is established by the module register.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: What would establish a specific market boundary?

records.label: Audience question
records.prompt: Which people and organisations face this task?

records.label: Existing alternative
records.prompt: Manual notes or existing document practices may be enough.

records.label: Market evidence gap
records.prompt: No market size, demand or competitive research supplied.

pages.title: How could the model earn revenue?
pages.lead: The commercial hypothesis is that a defined service could be valuable under sustainable payment conditions. We have not established the offering, price, buyer or acquisition route. Activity, interest and revenue are different categories, and none should be substituted for another.
pages.body: Follow-up: what exactly would someone pay for? This script includes no transaction, signed contract, revenue forecast or statement of actual willingness to pay.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: Which evidence would be most useful before discussing a revenue model?

records.label: Offering hypothesis
records.prompt: A defined offering could be explored as a hypothesis.

records.label: Buyer question
records.prompt: Who would choose it, and under which conditions?

records.label: Payment evidence needed
records.prompt: No price, contracts, invoices or revenue supplied.

pages.title: Who is responsible for the work?
pages.lead: The work would need product judgement, implementation and contextual review. Those are role categories, not appointments. A real team discussion should identify confirmed experience, involvement and gaps without borrowing credibility from invented biographies or unverified endorsements.
pages.body: Follow-up: which capability is missing? Replace role labels with people only when their involvement and relevant background are confirmed.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: Which missing responsibility could block the next useful step?

records.label: Confirmed role information
records.prompt: No named appointments or verified team experience supplied.

records.label: Capability gap
records.prompt: Product, technical and inquiry responsibilities need definition.

records.label: Appointment to verify
records.prompt: Check availability, authority and relevant experience before sharing.

pages.title: What are you asking investors to support?
pages.lead: In this fictional conversation, the request is to examine the learning plan and the evidence it would need. No real funding amount, valuation, security, runway or agreed terms are supplied. A genuine financing request would need its own verified context and appropriate review.
pages.body: Follow-up: what decision should the next artifact enable? Keep an invitation to discuss separate from a securities offer or an implication that funding is committed.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: What would turn a broad resource request into an inspectable plan?

records.label: Discussion request
records.prompt: Discuss support for resolving the next evidence gap.

records.label: Learning purpose
records.prompt: Define and inspect a bounded learning activity.

records.label: Terms not supplied
records.prompt: No investment amount, valuation or agreed terms supplied.

pages.title: What could make this fail?
pages.lead: The problem may not matter enough, a simpler alternative may be better, or maintenance could outweigh the benefit. Those possibilities should be visible before a financing conversation becomes a persuasive story. We would want evidence that can change our view, not only confirm it.
pages.body: Follow-up: which result would make us stop or revise? The list is a discussion aid, not a complete risk assessment or a guarantee that other risks are absent.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: Which assumption would you test first if you wanted to challenge the concept?

records.label: Key assumption
records.prompt: People may not need the proposed shared-context interaction.

records.label: Disconfirming evidence
records.prompt: A credible alternative may solve the task more simply.

records.label: Revise condition
records.prompt: Revise or stop if appropriate inquiry rejects the premise.

pages.title: What difficult question remains unanswered?
pages.lead: The hardest question is whether the proposed structure improves a real task enough to justify adoption and maintenance. We cannot answer that from this template. A useful response is to name the gap, explain why it matters and identify the next appropriate source.
pages.body: Follow-up: what would we bring back to a second conversation? An unanswered question should stay open rather than being disguised as a confident forecast.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: Which answer should be deferred until evidence exists?

records.label: Unanswered question
records.prompt: Whether the concept addresses a sufficiently useful task.

records.label: Why it matters
records.prompt: Without that evidence, build and business claims are premature.

records.label: Next source
records.prompt: An appropriately scoped task observation or concept review.

pages.title: What happens after this conversation?
pages.lead: We would record the questions raised, confirm who is responsible for any next discussion and identify a suitable artifact to review. That is not a promise of a second meeting, a funding commitment or a completed diligence process. The useful outcome is a clearer evidence request.
pages.body: Follow-up: what may be shared and with whom? Real confidentiality, rights and investment arrangements need their own authorised processes outside this fictional brief.
pages.subheading: Speaker / evidence note — not a performance claim
pages.detail: Keep the fictional status visible. Replace illustrative material only with appropriately sourced, verified information; proposed questions are not completed diligence.
pages.question: What exact response would make a next conversation worthwhile?

records.label: Question to carry forward
records.prompt: Which uncertainty deserves the next bounded inquiry?

records.label: Responsibility to confirm
records.prompt: Agree who can obtain and review the appropriate evidence.

records.label: Sharing boundary
records.prompt: No real meeting, commitment or permission to share implied.
